title: potentilla bolanderi var. clevelandii
intro: Potentilla bolanderi var. clevelandii, commonly known as Cleveland's potentilla or Cleveland's cinquefoil, is a plant species within the rose family (Rosaceae) that is native to the southwestern United States and Mexico. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, making it a valuable resource for treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents present in Potentilla bolanderi var. clevelandii include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as reducing inflammation, fighting off infections, and protecting against oxidative stress. The plant's therapeutic actions are thought to be due to its ability to scavenge free radicals, modulate immune responses, and exhibit anti-cancer and cardioprotective effects.
